title: Relative undercategories create preserved limits
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, coherent cones and limits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $A,B$ be quasicategories in a common sufficiently large universe, $G:A\to B$ a simplicial functor and $b\in B$ a vertex. Form the degreewise pullback
$$C_b=\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B,G}A,$$
with projection $U:C_b\to A$. Its vertices are pairs $(a,\eta:b\to G(a))$. It is the quasicategory $E$ of [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] for the cospan $\Delta^0\xrightarrow{\,b\,}B\xleftarrow{\,G\,}A$, with $U$ its target projection. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $d:K\to C_b$. Suppose $Ud$ has a limiting cone in $A$ and $G$ carries that cone to a limiting cone in $B$. Then $d$ has a limiting coherent cone in $C_b$ whose image under $U$ is equivalent, as a cone on the fixed diagram $Ud$, to the given one. The statement includes $K=\varnothing$. No conservativity, approximation or fibration hypothesis on $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 (Kerodon Tag 02KB), limit creation in a coslice, and Corollary 4.6.8.18 for its mapping-space fiber formula. Agent-formulated relative pullback/arrow-model version for an arbitrary functor G; these source results do not literally state that version. Read the statements and proofs online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text:
Put $A_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,A)$, $B_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ and $D=Ud$. Uncurrying the arrow coordinate of $d$ gives a coherent transformation $\beta:\Delta_K b\to GD$. More generally there is an exact simplicial identification
$$\operatorname{Fun}(K,C_b)=\{\Delta_Kb\}\times_{B_K,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B_K)\times_{\mathrm{ev}_1,B_K,G_K}A_K.$$
Indeed, in degree $n$ both sides consist of a map $K\times\Delta^n\to A$ and a map $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to B$, with the same two endpoint equations. Swapping the last two factors identifies their coordinates, and restriction in $\Delta^n$ identifies every simplicial operator. This argument also identifies the constant diagram at $(a,\alpha)$ with $(\Delta_Ka,\Delta_K\alpha)$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text:
The comma statement makes $C_b$ a quasicategory, and the functor calculus makes $A_K,B_K,\operatorname{Fun}(K,C_b)$ quasicategories with Kan mapping spaces. Apply the comma mapping formula both to $C_b$ and to the presentation in step 1. For $x=(a,\alpha:b\to Ga)$ and an arbitrary $c=(L,\eta:b\to GL)$ it gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{C_b}(x,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_A(a,L)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_B(b,GL)}\{\eta\},$$
$$N_x:=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,C_b)}(\Delta_Kx,d)\simeq T_a\times^h_Z\{\beta\},$$
where $T_a=\operatorname{Map}_{A_K}(\Delta_Ka,D)$ and $Z=\operatorname{Map}_{B_K}(\Delta_Kb,GD)$. The first maps to the bases are $f\mapsto G(f)\alpha$ and $t\mapsto G_K(t)\Delta_K\alpha$, respectively. The missing source-endpoint factor in each formula is $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^0}(*,*)=\Delta^0$. These equivalences respect the actual projections to $\operatorname{Map}_A(a,L)$ and $T_a$, and respect composition by pasting coherent squares, as specified in the comma statement.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text:
Write the given limiting cone as $\lambda:\Delta_K L\to D$. Since $G\lambda$ is limiting, the mapping-space criterion for a limit, applied in $B$ at the test object $b$, says that
$$q:\operatorname{Map}_B(b,GL)\longrightarrow Z,\qquad \eta\longmapsto(G\lambda)\Delta_K\eta$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The fiber criterion says that its homotopy fiber over the vertex $\beta$ is contractible, hence has a vertex. Choose its data $\eta:b\to GL$ and a path $\theta:q(\eta)\simeq\beta$. These are coherent mapping-space data, not a strictly commuting triangle. This supplies the candidate apex $c=(L,\eta)$ in $C_b$. All mapping spaces here are Kan by the functor calculus.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text: For $x=c$, the point of $T_L\times^h_Z\{\beta\}$ given by $(\lambda,\theta)$ has a preimage on components under the second equivalence in step 2. Choose a vertex in that component of $N_c$; its edge is an actual coherent cone $h:\Delta_Kc\to d$. Compatibility with the projection to $T_L$ gives a path from $\mu:=Uh$ to $\lambda$ in $T_L$. To see why a single path can be used, a component equality gives a finite edge zigzag; reverse edges and compose adjacent edges by two-dimensional Kan horn fillers. Postcomposition by $\mu$ and by $\lambda$ on every $\operatorname{Map}_A(a,L)$ is therefore homotopic: apply coherent composition to this path and the constant-diagram map. The same applies to $G\mu,G\lambda$ in $B_K$. By the composition lemma and the limit mapping criterion, $\mu$ and $G\mu$ are limiting cones. This verifies limit preservation for the actual cone just chosen, without demanding that a comparison equivalence lift a specified vertex strictly.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text:
Fix any $x=(a,\alpha)$ as in step 2. Postcomposition by $\mu$ gives a weak equivalence $r_a:\operatorname{Map}_A(a,L)\to T_a$, and postcomposition by $G\mu$ gives a weak equivalence $s:\operatorname{Map}_B(b,GL)\to Z$, by the two limit criteria of step 4. The square of the maps $f\mapsto G(f)\alpha$ and $t\mapsto G_K(t)\Delta_K\alpha$ commutes up to the coherent associativity homotopy. The cone $h$ supplies the other side homotopy $s(\eta)\simeq\beta$. Thus $r_a,s$ and the identity of the point compare the two homotopy-pullback spans of step 2. Apply the homotopy-coherent cube invariance statement to these spans (its auxiliary square domains may both be empty, so the cube coherence condition there is vacuous). It makes the induced map between their path homotopy pullbacks an equivalence. Under the natural comma formulas this is precisely postcomposition
$$\operatorname{Map}_{C_b}(x,c)\longrightarrow N_x,\qquad v\longmapsto h\Delta_Kv.$$
Indeed its first coordinate is $\mu\Delta_K(Uv)$; its path coordinate pastes the comma square of $v$ with that of $h$. This is the pasting compatibility asserted in the comma node, including all higher simplices. Coherent composition provides the displayed associativity homotopy. Consequently the actual postcomposition map is a weak equivalence, not merely a bijection on components.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text: The functor-cone mapping criterion in the quasicategory $C_b$ now says that $h$ is limiting, since step 5 applies to every vertex $x$ of $C_b$. Its image is the limiting cone $\mu$ on the fixed diagram $D$. The given $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are terminal objects in the same coherent cone category $(\Delta_K\downarrow D)$. The functor calculus says that its full subcategory of terminal objects is a contractible Kan complex. They are therefore equivalent as cones on this fixed diagram. This proves exactly the asserted comparison with the originally supplied cone.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.4.26 motivates limit creation; the following is an agent proof for the relative arrow model using the cited general mapping-space statements, not a quotation of that proposition.

proof.text: For $K=\varnothing$, both $A_K$ and $B_K$ are the one-point simplicial set by the internal-functor definition. Thus $T_a=Z=\Delta^0$, while the hypothesis says that $L$ and $GL$ are terminal in $A$ and $B$. In particular the same map $q$ of step 3 is an equivalence to a point and supplies $\eta$; step 5 has contractible target $N_x=\Delta^0$ and proves that $c$ is terminal. All coordinate identifications and mapping-space arguments above remain valid. No nonemptiness of $K$, reflection of equivalences, approximation property or fibration property of $G$ entered the proof.
